clue.text: Cabbage work-rate, perhaps, of the beetles

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage, as in coleslaw
OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of rate may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether cabbage affects how hard beetles work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns RATE into TERA. 'work-rate' reads as one idea but splits into OP and the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleoptera is the zoological order containing all beetles.

clue.text: Grainless tropic island

indicators.note: less means without, so the grain is taken away from the tropic

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is one of the two tropics
corn is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A tropical island where no cereal grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grainless' looks like one adjective but splits: CORN taken out of CAPRICORN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Merry and bright

explanation.surface: A description of a cheerful, sunny disposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightsome means both light-hearted and cheerful, and also luminous or full of light.

clue.text: Machine for which barmaid need not give change

indicators.note: to give change here means to alter, so these fourteen letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slot machine that saves the barmaid handing out coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give change' looks like a till matter, but it signals the anagram of BARMAID NEED NOT; a fruit machine pays out itself, so the barmaid need not give change.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine is nicknamed for its single lever arm and its habit of robbing players.

clue.text: Strong bands, not elastic

parts.note: the clue describes tough fibrous cords in the body that join muscle to bone and do not stretch, unlike rubber bands

explanation.surface: Sturdy straps that do not stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the inelastic connective cords that attach muscles to bones.

clue.text: Brave, having symptom of erythema

explanation.surface: A warrior whose skin shows a medical condition.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' is an old (now offensive) term for a Native American warrior; erythema is reddening of the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive word for a Native American warrior; literally, reddened skin is what erythema causes.

clue.text: Home fixture for City

explanation.surface: A home match scheduled for a team called City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixture' suggests a football match, but here it is something plumbed into a house. Bath is a city in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a fitting in a bathroom; Bath is also a Roman spa city in south-west England.

clue.text: Confess one's escaped from Maidstone somehow

indicators.note: escaped from means the letters of one's get away, leaving the rest of the town name
somehow tells us the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Maidstone is the county town of Kent
taken as written, its four letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having broken out of Maidstone prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ONES from MAIDSTONE ('escaped from') to leave MAIDT, and 'somehow' rearranges it. Maidstone, in Kent, has a well-known prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to acknowledge or own up to it.

clue.text: Countryman presenting his ears?

parts.note: ears here are the heads of corn, so a farm worker brings in the grain crop rather than showing his own ears

explanation.surface: A rural man showing off his ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm labourer or machine gathers in the ripe grain at the end of summer.

clue.text: Bur to irritate

parts.note: the word Bur is the verb rub written backwards, which is what the answer phrase literally describes

explanation.surface: A prickly seed case is good at annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: A bur clings and annoys, but the clue's point is that BUR is RUB written the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to stroke their feelings against the grain, as with a cat's fur.

clue.text: Short-backed college servant is down-at-heel

indicators.note: backed means the servant's title is turned round, read from the back

parts.note: a gyp is a college servant at Cambridge
shabby and poor, which is mean

explanation.surface: A college servant with a short back is looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-backed' reads as one adjective; split it so 'Short' is the definition and 'backed' reverses GYP to PYG.
explanation.definitionFit: Pygmean is an old adjective meaning dwarfish or very small in stature.

clue.text: Salesman in charge of the kettle department

definitions.text: in charge of the kettle department

explanation.surface: A sales rep running the shop's kettle section.
explanation.walkthrough: In America a drummer is a travelling salesman; 'kettle' refers to kettledrums, not tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Drummer is old US slang for a commercial traveller; and a percussionist plays the timpani or kettledrums.

clue.text: Get engaged to make synchronising mechanism

explanation.surface: An instruction to engage parts so a mechanism works in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' tempts thoughts of marriage, but it means gears meshing together.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts that mesh fit together; a device of that name prevents operations happening out of step.

clue.text: It has to go back before the tenth

indicators.note: before places the reversed word ahead of the next piece
to go back means the word It is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something must return before the tenth day of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns IT into TI, placed 'before' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce or income paid to the church.

clue.text: Disappear from Barchester. Towers?

explanation.surface: Someone vanishing from Trollope's cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: To slope off is to sneak away. Obadiah Slope is the scheming chaplain in Anthony Trollope's novel Barchester Towers; the full stop splits the title.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave furtively is to sidle off; Mr Slope is a character in a Victorian novel set in a cathedral town.

clue.text: This fastener makes us secure, work in' in office

parts.note: secure means safe
office work is typing; with the dropped g of workin', it becomes typin'

explanation.surface: A fastener that keeps us secure while we work in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'workin'' tells you to drop the G from TYPING too.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent pin with a covered clasp, used to fasten cloth, is the item meant.

clue.text: It is designed to stop beans over-baking

definitions.text: It is designed to stop beans over-baking

parts.words: It is designed to stop beans over-baking
parts.note: bean is slang for head, so this is headgear that keeps a head from overheating in strong sunshine, not a kitchen gadget

explanation.surface: A kitchen device that keeps beans from overcooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet or topee protected colonial travellers' heads from tropical heat.

clue.text: This is meant to show the correct time in bars

definitions.text: This is meant to show the correct time in bars

parts.words: This is meant to show the correct time in bars
parts.note: bars are musical measures, so this device ticks out the tempo for a musician rather than telling drinkers the hour

explanation.surface: A clock for pubs that shows the right time.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticking device with a pendulum sets the tempo for practising music.

clue.text: Side above water release directors

parts.note: to release is to free
the directors of a company form its board

explanation.surface: Company directors released on the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, this is the height of hull between the waterline and the deck.

clue.text: He approves of true accounts

parts.note: a person who checks company books and signs them off as correct, rather than someone who likes honest stories

explanation.surface: A person who likes stories that are true.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional examines financial records and certifies that they are accurate.

clue.text: Elaborate work in the dark

explanation.surface: Someone working on something elaborate in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to processing photographic film in a darkroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand on an idea is one sense; processing exposed film into negatives in a darkroom is the other.

clue.text: Moving arm in two directions

indicators.note: in two directions says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An arm that can move both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part, like a helicopter blade or a distributor arm, spins round a shaft.

clue.text: Harmful substance found in canned beef

indicators.note: in places the beef inside the can

parts.note: canned food comes in a tin
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: Something poisonous discovered in tinned beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' supplies TIN, and 'in' puts OX inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison, often one produced by bacteria in spoiled food.

clue.text: Hospital's cross beams?

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Wooden cross-beams in a hospital roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-beams' looks like timber but splits into X and RAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiographs taken in a hospital use penetrating radiation to image bones.

clue.text: Vendor apt to renovate such sale room piece?

indicators.note: to renovate is to make over, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seller is keen to restore an item for the auction room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to renovate' rearranges VENDOR APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A writing desk with a sloping top, or in America a large sofa, is antique furniture often found at auction.

clue.text: Opinion of English into Spanish wine

indicators.note: into places the English letter inside the wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red wine from Spain

explanation.surface: An English view on Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine, from tinto.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true.

clue.text: Holy character and sort of saint this musician

parts.note: pi is a Greek character, and also school slang for pious or holy

indicators.note: sort of hints that the letters of saint are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A musician who is both a holy figure and a kind of saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SAINT into ANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays the piano at a keyboard is the musician meant.

clue.text: Ron gets duck — lbw — out to such a poor delivery

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a cricket score of nothing, O
taken as written; leg before wicket in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Ron is out for nought, lbw, to a bad ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero; lbw (leg before wicket) is a way of being out. 'out' rearranges RON, O and LBW; 'delivery' means birth, not a bowled ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of humble birth, the delivery here is a child's arrival, not a cricket ball.

clue.text: Capital architect using northern wood

parts.note: ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: An architect from the capital working in northern timber.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash designed much of Regency London, including Regent Street, hence 'Capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash shaped Regency London with terraces and Regent Street.

clue.text: Deposit New York paper met somehow

indicators.note: somehow tells us the letters are put together in some other order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York newspaper met a down payment somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges NY with PAPER and MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid up front, in advance of delivery, is the sense of deposit here.
